intended_object: For a morphism of schemes f : X → Y and opens V ⊆ f⁻¹(U), the canonical isomorphism, in the arrow category, between the stalk map at x ∈ V of the restricted morphism f.resLE U V : V → U and the stalk map of f at x (docstring).
explanation: The definition builds an Arrow isomorphism. On the target side it uses `V.stalkIso x`, the standard identification of the stalk of an open subscheme with the stalk of the ambient scheme. On the source side it uses `U.stalkIso` composed with `stalkCongr`, which handles the fact that the image point of x in U is only propositionally equal to f x in Y. Commutativity of the square is proved from `resLE_comp_ι` and the fact that stalk maps compose, so this is the canonical isomorphism and not merely some isomorphism. The setting is fully general (arbitrary schemes, opens and points), and the definition matches its docstring. It is a small infrastructure isomorphism, but it encodes a genuine canonical identification, which is why I treat it as a mathematical object.
